probe.label: Direct call

cases.label: addAll into a total that is not zero
cases.calls: A total starting at 100, then addAll on {1, 2, 3}, on {10, -4} and on an empty vector in turn — the same variable every time. Then a total starting at -5. Then ten thousand values of a million, which is the size the constraints allow.

explanation:
## The program

```cpp
void addAll(const std::vector<int>& values, long long& total)
{
    for (int value : values) total += value;
}

long long total{};
addAll(evens, total);
addAll(odds, total);
```

## += against =

This is the whole behavioural difference, and it is one character:

```cpp
total += value;     // contributes; two calls accumulate
total = sum;        // reports; the second call overwrites the first
```

Both are defensible functions and they are not interchangeable. The
name has to say which: `addAll` adds, and a function called
`sumOf` or `computeTotal` had better set. Reference parameters make
this ambiguity possible, which is one honest argument against them —
a function that returns its answer cannot be unclear about it.

## In-out parameters

The `total` parameter is neither purely input nor purely output: it
is read and written, and its incoming value matters. That is why it
cannot be `const`, and why passing a literal is impossible:

```cpp
addAll(evens, 0);           // will not compile
```

A non-const reference cannot bind to a temporary, which is the
language stopping you from writing to something that is about to
stop existing. `const long long&` would bind, and then the function
could not add to it anyway.

## Why the design is slightly dubious

Worth saying plainly: returning the sum is usually better.

```cpp
long long sumOf(const std::vector<int>& values);

long long total{ sumOf(evens) + sumOf(odds) };
```

The function then has no side effect, can be called in an
expression, and cannot be misused by forgetting to initialise the
accumulator. The accumulator form earns its place when the thing
being built up is expensive to copy — appending to a large vector
or a string rather than returning a new one each time.

A good exercise is not always a good design, and saying which is
which is part of teaching it.

## Positions count from zero

The first element is at position 0, which is even, so it goes in
`evens`. "First, third, fifth" and "positions 0, 2, 4" are the same
set described from different starting points, and the statement
says both so that there is nothing to guess.

## What this does not check

Whether `total` was initialised. `long long total;` without the `{}`
is indeterminate, and `addAll` would add to rubbish — producing a
wrong answer with no bad behaviour to notice. That is the standing
cost of an accumulator parameter, and the reason the braces on
`long long total{};` are not optional.
